Class LessonValidationTestingAutomation

java.lang.Object
testingAutomation.LessonValidationTestingAutomation
public class LessonValidationTestingAutomation extends Object

Title: LessonValidationTestingAutomation Class.

Description: Semi-automated tests for LessonInputPolicy, the rules that LessonsLearned.create and LessonsLearned.update apply before anything is written. The suite covers two Contributor requirements:

  • CS-10: title, category, description, and contributor are required; resolution and keywords are optional. An empty or whitespace-only required value is refused with a message that names the field.
  • CS-11: title 80, category 30, description 2000, resolution 2000, keywords 200 characters, at most 10 keywords of at most 30 characters each. A value over its limit is refused with a message that names the field.

Each test is one private method, named after its test id, whose Javadoc states the requirement, the input used, and the condition for a Pass. Boundary values are tested on both sides: the largest accepted value is a positive test and one character more is a negative test. A negative test passes only when the refusal carries the expected problem title, so a refusal for the wrong reason is reported as a Failure.

How to read the output: one line per test, "Pass:" or "Failure:", followed by the test id, what was checked, and the requirement. The last line gives the totals for the suite. Every id appears in "Requirements to Tests Map.pdf".

    • val01TitleAccepted

      private static void val01TitleAccepted()

      VAL-01 (CS-10, positive). A normal title is accepted.

      How: validateTitle is given a 41-character title. It returns null only when the title is present and within 80 characters.

      Pass when: validateTitle returns null.

    • val03WhitespaceTitleRefused

      private static void val03WhitespaceTitleRefused()

      VAL-03 (CS-10, negative). A title of spaces only is refused.

      How: validateTitle is given three spaces. This catches a check that tests for an empty string but forgets to trim, which would accept a title the list shows as blank.

    • val12DescriptionAt300Accepted

      private static void val12DescriptionAt300Accepted()

      VAL-12 (CS-11, positive). A 300-character description is accepted.

      How: validateDescription is given 300 copies of "x". This is the regression test for the HW2 defect: the HW2 code used InputLimits.checkLength, whose 256-character ceiling refused every description from 257 to 2000 characters. LessonInputPolicy now uses checkLongText for the two long fields.

      Pass when: validateDescription returns null.

    • val19ValidKeywordsAccepted

      private static void val19ValidKeywordsAccepted()

      VAL-19 (CS-11, positive). Four short keywords are accepted.

      How: validateKeywords is given "H2, database, JDBC, lock": under 200 characters, under 10 keywords, and each keyword under 30 characters.

      Pass when: validateKeywords returns null.

    • val20ElevenKeywordsRefused

      private static void val20ElevenKeywordsRefused()

      VAL-20 (CS-11, negative). Eleven keywords are refused.

      How: validateKeywords is given "a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h,i,j,k", one more than the limit of 10. The string is only 21 characters, so the refusal can only come from the count.

      Pass when: the problem returned is "There are too many keywords".

    • val25FullLessonWithBlankTitleRefused

      private static void val25FullLessonWithBlankTitleRefused()

      VAL-25 (CS-10, negative). validateLesson refuses a lesson whose only fault is an empty title, which shows the per-field rule is applied when the whole lesson is checked.

      How: validateLesson is given the VAL-24 values with the title replaced by "".

      Pass when: the problem returned is "The title is required".

    • refusedWith

      private static boolean refusedWith(validation.LessonInputPolicy.Problem problem, String expectedTitle)

      Method: refusedWith

      Description: True when a problem was returned and its title is the one expected. Checking the title, not just that something was refused, means a value refused for the wrong reason is reported as a Failure.

      Parameters:
      problem - what the validation method returned
      expectedTitle - the problem title the requirement calls for
      Returns:
      true when the refusal is the expected one

    • check

      private static void check(String label, boolean result)

      Method: check

      Description: Records one test outcome. Prints "Pass:" or "Failure:" followed by the label, and updates numPassed or numFailed. The format matches the TP1 suites, so every suite reads the same way in the TestingScreencast.

      Parameters:
      label - the test id, what was checked, and the requirement
      result - true when the behaviour matched the requirement
